## Objective
- Finish the existing Neon Coast game as a complete, playable game and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Build it now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Continued the existing Three.js city/patrol game rather than replacing it.
- Added a playable patrol mission with driving, on-foot movement, firing, threats, and HUD updates.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js` with a full implementation including city scene, player vehicle/agent, hostile cars, pulse combat, mission progress, minimap, HUD updates, pause/day-night toggles, and keyboard/touch event handlers.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Installed Playwright Chromium after browser launch initially failed because it was missing.

### Active
- Validate rendered gameplay and interactions in Playwright; save and inspect a latest small JPEG screenshot.
- Fix any discovered browser/runtime or gameplay issues.

### Blocked
- Browser validation has not yet been rerun after installing Chromium.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:8000` with `playwright-cli` and inspect browser errors/runtime state.
2. Check loading/overlay behavior: `.hidden` was not found in `style.css`, while the game code uses it to hide the loader and help pill.
3. Exercise driving, firing, entering/exiting, pause, and mission progress; fix issues found.
4. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot, then summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: main game implementation, recently replaced.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game UI, element IDs, and Three.js import map.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: existing HUD and responsive styling; check for missing `.hidden` rules.

## Important Context
- A Python HTTP server was started for `http://localhost:8000`; its shell command timed out, so confirm the endpoint is still available before browser testing.
- No changes were committed.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Neon Coast game as a playable game and verify it in-browser.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification, make reasonable assumptions, and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Continued the existing Three.js city/patrol game rather than replacing it.
- Added a patrol mission with driving, on-foot movement, pulse combat, threats, and HUD updates.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `game.js` with the game implementation: city scene, player vehicle/agent, hostile cars, pulse combat, mission progress, minimap, HUD, pause/day-night toggles, and keyboard/touch handlers.
- Added `.hidden{display:none!important}` to `style.css`, fixing loader/help visibility.
- Started a local server at `http://localhost:8000`; page loads and renders in Playwright.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest small edit.
- Confirmed loader is hidden and no game runtime errors appeared; console only showed a missing favicon 404 and WebGL performance warnings.

### Active
- Finish browser interaction checks and fix issues found.
- Verify mobile/touch controls, then capture and inspect a latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Browser key simulation reported stationary speed (`000`) and `ON FOOT`; driving input may need investigation. No screenshot has yet been captured.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://localhost:8000`; determine why the attempted keyboard sequence left the player on foot and stationary.
2. Check driving, firing, entering/exiting, pause, and mission progress; test touch controls.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js`, capture a JPEG at ≤1280px viewport width, and inspect only that latest screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: main game implementation and recent touch-stick element references.
- `style.css`: HUD/responsive styles; `.hidden` rule was added.
- `index.html`: UI element IDs, canvas, and Three.js import map.

## Important Context
- Playwright opens successfully, and the loading overlay reaches `display: none`.
- A browser sequence of W movement, E, Space, and Escape returned `speed: "000"`, `mode: "ON FOOT"`, `mission: "0 / 8"`, and pause overlay `grid`; input testing needs to be repeated and diagnosed.
- The latest edit added `stickZone` and `stickKnob` DOM references to `game.js`; touch-stick behavior has not been implemented or verified.
- Changes are uncommitted.
